title: README: a simpler architecture diagram
lede: No runtime code changes. The README's architecture diagram had grown to 10 nodes and 16 labelled edges, most of them repeating the numbered sections below it. It now shows only the shape: a thin UI, a press flowing through the pure core, and components reading the stores through selectors.

files.question: What does the diagram still show?
files.summary: 8 nodes and 10 edges: the Press DOM side feeds the Press, which drives the Drag controller and geometry; both call the stores; components call actions and read through selectors; Editing ending saves the Draft text.
files.owns: The one-glance picture of the architecture.
files.never: Repeats per-selector labels, the separate Board, Note and Toolbar nodes, or the rules between the two stores: those stay in sections 1 to 5.
files.tested: Not tested: check the diagram renders in GitHub's file view.

steps.title: A reader opens the Architecture section
steps.explain: The two subgraphs say where the decisions are: the UI only passes **Press** events in and draws what the **Drag** controller sends back through `DragIO`. Solid arrows are calls, dotted ones are selector subscriptions, and the thick arrow is the Notes store saving the **Draft text** when **Editing** ends, as the unchanged caption says.

notes.title: Details moved out of the diagram, not lost
notes.detail: The Board attaching the Press DOM side once, `DragHandlers`, Undo and the Current colour and size are all still described in sections 1 to 3. The counter-argument: a reader who only looks at the picture now sees less of the wiring.
